text_blocks.snippet: A princess braid is a hairstyle that typically involves a French braid (or a variation like a Dutch braid) that wraps around the head, resembling a crown or headband. It's often characterized by a loose, romantic look, and can be adorned with flowers or other decorative elements.
snippet_highlighted_words: a hairstyle that typically involves a French braid (or a variation like a Dutch braid) that wraps around the head, resembling a crown or headband

text_blocks.snippet: This video demonstrates how to create a princess braid with a simple pull-through technique:

list.snippet: The princess braid often starts with a French braid (or a Dutch braid) that begins at the hairline, usually near the forehead or temples.
The braid can be a regular three-strand braid or a variation like a rope twist braid.
The key is to incorporate strands of hair as you braid, bringing the braid around the head's perimeter.
As you braid, you'll continue adding hair from the sides of your head, effectively weaving the braid around your hairline.
The braid can be a full circle around the head or just a partial crown, depending on preference.
Once the braid reaches the starting point or the desired length, it's secured with an elastic or bobby pins.
To enhance the princess aesthetic, the braid can be slightly loosened or textured by pulling at the strands.
Decorative elements like flowers, ribbons, or small clips can be added for a more elaborate look.
French Rope Twist: A variation where the braid is created using a rope twist technique, resulting in a thicker, more textured braid.
Dutch Braid: A braid where the strands are crossed under instead of over, giving it a raised, "inverted" look.
Partial Crown: The braid only goes halfway around the head, creating a half-crown effect.

text_blocks.snippet: Peekaboo braids are a fun and trendy hairstyle where contrasting colored hair extensions are braided into sections of your hair, typically underneath the top layer, so they "peek" out from underneath. This creates a playful pop of color and a unique look, allowing for creative expression through different color combinations and placement.
snippet_highlighted_words: a fun and trendy hairstyle where contrasting colored hair extensions are braided into sections of your hair, typically underneath the top layer, so they "peek" out from underneath

text_blocks.snippet: This video demonstrates how to do peekaboo braids:

list.title: Hidden Highlights:
list.snippet: Peekaboo braids are essentially a way to add highlights, but instead of subtle strands, you're using braids with extensions that are strategically hidden within the hair.

list.title: Color Contrast:
list.snippet: The key is the contrast between the natural hair color and the color of the extensions. This contrast is what makes the peekaboo effect noticeable.

list.title: Versatile Placement:
list.snippet: You can choose where you want the peekaboo braids to appear. They can be near the nape of the neck, along the sides, or anywhere else you desire, according to Byrdie.

list.title: Creative Freedom:
list.snippet: There's a lot of room for creativity. You can experiment with different colors, including vibrant shades or more subtle tones, and you can decide how many peekaboo braids you want.

list.title: Protective Style:
list.snippet: Peekaboo braids can also be a protective style, as they can help minimize damage from heat styling and other styling practices.
